item.case_name: Fact piece about a real thing
item.title: Voyager One Against the References

turns.text: Make a silent 9-second widescreen fact clip about Voyager 1, using NASA's mission page as the reference: https://science.nasa.gov/mission/voyager/voyager-1/ . Three equal-length scenes: 'Launched: September 5, 1977', 'Jupiter flyby: 1979', 'Saturn flyby: 1980'. Keep 'Voyager 1' and 'Source: NASA Science' visible. Show the probe near Earth, Jupiter, then Saturn; match its real dish-and-boom design. Don't mix in Voyager 2's Uranus or Neptune visits.

item.tests: Tests whether a factual film matches a named reference in dates, mission identity, spacecraft appearance and scene order.

answer_sheet.Facts to include: Voyager 1 launched September 5, 1977, flew by Jupiter in 1979 and flew by Saturn in 1980.
answer_sheet.Length and scene order: 9 seconds total: three 3-second scenes showing Earth, Jupiter and Saturn in that order.
answer_sheet.Wording: Use exactly the five supplied labels. Keep Voyager 1 and Source: NASA Science visible throughout.
answer_sheet.Sound: Completely silent, with no narration, music or sound effects.
answer_sheet.Visual style: Your call, provided the spacecraft matches the real dish-and-boom design and the planets are recognizable.

must_haves: Three scenes appear in order, each lasting approximately three seconds: probe near Earth, near Jupiter, then near Saturn.
Each scene displays its corresponding date caption exactly, with 'Voyager 1' and 'Source: NASA Science' visible throughout.
The probe consistently has Voyager's large circular communications dish and projecting instrument booms, not solar-panel wings or a generic satellite body.
Jupiter is visibly banded and Saturn has prominent rings; neither is replaced with Uranus or Neptune.
The output contains no Uranus or Neptune flyby claims and no conflicting dates.

dialog.agent:
**I haven’t run a generation or spent any credits.** The connected tools don’t expose a price estimator or account-balance check, so I can’t give you a verified credit quote before running—and I won’t submit a job to find out.

### Lowest-cost approach
For this fact clip, **three still images with simple pans and text overlays** would be more reliable than AI-generated video:
- Exact 3-second scenes and readable captions.
- A genuine NASA spacecraft image can preserve Voyager 1’s dish-and-boom design.
- Assembling existing NASA imagery in a free video editor can use **0 Magic Hour generation credits**. That editing workflow isn’t available through my connected tools here.

### Magic Hour alternative
A **silent, 9-second, 16:9 video at 480p using LTX 2.5** is within the listed free-plan model settings, though account-specific duration eligibility and cost still need confirmation. Generated text, precise scene timing, and spacecraft geometry aren’t guaranteed.

Cheaper options to price-check:
- **6 seconds:** three 2-second scenes.
- **3 seconds:** three 1-second scenes, but captions become difficult to read.
- **480p:** already the smallest available free-plan video resolution; muting audio doesn’t necessarily lower the price.

The planned sequence would be:

| Time | Visual | Exact caption |
|---|---|---|
| 0–3 s | Voyager 1 near Earth | Launched: September 5, 1977 |
| 3–6 s | Voyager 1 near Jupiter | Jupiter flyby: 1979 |
| 6–9 s | Voyager 1 near Saturn | Saturn flyby: 1980 |

**“Voyager 1”** and **“Source: NASA Science”** would remain visible throughout. No Uranus or Neptune visits.

I haven’t been able to open the linked NASA page with these tools, so I also can’t claim to have checked it directly. **My recommendation is the 9-second still-image edit rather than shortening the clip.** If you prefer Magic Hour generation, please obtain its displayed quote for silent LTX 2.5, 480p, 9 seconds before authorizing a run.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with the cheapest option you listed

| Time | Image | Caption |
|---|---|---|

| 3–6 s | Voyager spacecraft near Jupiter | Jupiter flyby: 1979 |
| 6–9 s | Voyager spacecraft near Saturn | Saturn flyby: 1980 |

Use NASA spacecraft imagery to preserve the real dish-and-boom design, with a gentle zoom on each still. Avoid imagery suggesting Voyager 1 visited Uranus or Neptune.
